citations.title: Admission standards
citations.requirement: Admit and retain only people whose needs the home may lawfully meet. Lists 13 people who may not be accepted or retained, including those needing continual medical or nursing care, chronically bedfast, chronic unmanaged incontinence, or danger to self or others. Requires a medical evaluation (DSS-3122) within 30 days before admission and at least every 12 months, and a written administrator interview. Applicants receive the admission agreement, rights statement, facility rules and Ombudsman/legal-services sheet at or before the interview, and may review the latest DOH inspection report. Requires persistent efforts at alternative placement when a resident can no longer be retained.

citations.title: Resident protections
citations.requirement: (a) Resident rights statement: posted, given at admission, reviewed annually, with 19 minimum rights. (b) Resident organizations. (c) Written grievance system with posting of the procedure. (d) Admission agreement content, including SSI/HR personal-allowance offer and refunds. (f) Termination: 30 days' written notice on a DOH form, list of free legal and advocacy services, copy to the regional office within 5 days, and a court proceeding if the resident objects.

citations.title: Resident funds and valuables
citations.requirement: Governs the operator's handling of resident funds and valuables. Section number and title confirmed from the Part 487 table of contents. Body text NOT fetched; confirm detail before citing a subdivision.

citations.title: Resident services
citations.requirement: (a) Minimum services: room, board, housekeeping, supervision, personal care, case management, activities. (d) Supervision duties, evacuations, missing-resident steps, emergency and illness response, death, suicide attempt and felony reporting, and the Incident Report triggers. (e) Personal care, including a ban on physical restraints and monthly weights. (f) Medication management: self-administration, staff assistance limits, secure storage, no injectables by staff (except licensed staff), no dose changes without physician authorization.

citations.title: Food service
citations.requirement: Food service standards for adult homes. Section number and title confirmed from the Part 487 table of contents. Body text NOT fetched; food staffing hours come from §487.9(j).

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: Orientation and in-service training with documentation (a)(3)-(5). Staffing schedules kept 12 months (a)(6). Personnel records (a)(7). Annual physician/PA/RN statement plus TB assessment (a)(8). Staff must speak, read and write English (a)(13). First-aid-trained person on duty at all times (a)(15). Notify the regional office within 3 business days of key vacancies (a)(16). Justice Center staff exclusion list check (a)(7), (a)(17). Administrator approval, hours and qualifications (c). Resident volunteers and employees (b). Supervision census table, personal care 3.75 hrs, housekeeping 1.0 hr and food service 2.0 hrs per resident per week ((f)-(j), per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Records and reports
citations.requirement: Resident and facility records (c)-(d). Quality assurance plan updated at least every two years, with a quality improvement committee meeting at least every six months (d)(5)(ix). Annual financial statement DSS-2963, quarterly statistical report, quarterly resident roster (e). Mandated forms (f). Postings (g). Retention (h): 3 years after death or discharge for individual records, 7 years for program, business and renewal records.

citations.title: Environmental standards
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: sprinklers throughout buildings of 25+ beds, bedroom minimums of 100 sq ft single and 160 sq ft double, 1 toilet per 6 and 1 bath per 10 residents, and a call system.

citations.title: Disaster and emergency planning
citations.requirement: DOH-approved written disaster and emergency plan. Monthly staff fire drills at varied times, with full and partial evacuation. Quarterly drills with residents, and one total evacuation every 12 months. Annual observation of a resident drill by fire authorities, a certified service agency or DOH. Drill records. Notify DOH by the next business day of a work stoppage, fire, loss of a fire system, no hot water or loss of essential services. HPN account with 24/7 contacts, kept current monthly.

citations.title: Reporting of reportable incidents
citations.requirement: Facilities subject to the Justice Center, and their mandated reporters, report a reportable incident to the Justice Center immediately on reasonable cause. The facility must start an investigation. These duties are in addition to the other reporting duties in Part 487.

citations.title: Enriched housing program personnel
citations.requirement: For enriched housing programs: program coordinator hours, case manager 0.5 hr per resident per week, and 6 hrs per resident per week of combined personal care, housekeeping and food staff (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Enriched housing resident services (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced in 10 NYCRR 1001.10(l)(1) for medication (488.7(d)) and 1001.10(i) for case management (488.7(e)) when the ALR is certified as an enriched housing program. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: ALP resident services and services in the capitated rate
citations.requirement: Defines ALP resident services and the services covered by the Medicaid capitated rate (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: ALP personnel
citations.requirement: Designated individual, qualified case manager, and minimum staffing at the §487.9(f)(6) levels (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Applications for ALR licensure and EALR/SNALR certification
citations.requirement: Must also hold an adult home or enriched housing certificate. 60-day response rule. ALR approval lapses if the residence is not licensed and operating within 1 year. Licensure fee rules (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: ALR admission/individualized service plan provisions (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced in 1001.10(c) and (j)(1) as the source of the individualized service plan (ISP) requirement (cited there as 1001.7(h) and (k)). Title and text NOT fetched. Confirm the subdivision before citing.

citations.title: ALR residency agreement provisions (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced in 1001.10(c)-(d) (1001.8(f)) as the source of the signed residency agreement that must list services and additional charges. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Resident services (ALR)
citations.requirement: Minimum ALR services: housing, 24-hour on-site monitoring, daily food service, case management, ISP, and personal care and/or home care. Residents may use outside providers and choose their own health care providers. Case management duties include evaluation before admission and at least every 12 months using the DOH personal data and resident evaluation form. Health services come from an Article 36 home care agency unless EALR/SNALR-approved. Hospice permitted without EALR when conditions are met. Medication policies must meet 18 NYCRR 487.7(f)/488.7(d). Medication assistance record and PRN rules. EALR and SNALR service rules, including the 24-hour skilled nursing retention exception.

citations.title: Personnel (ALR)
citations.requirement: Case manager on site at least 20 hrs/week under 25 beds, scaled up to 40 hrs/week at 45+ beds. Resident aides: 40 hrs initial training, 12 hrs annual in-service, and an annual performance assessment with direct observation. Orientation topics and written job descriptions. Bloodborne pathogen exposure program and post-exposure procedure. EALR/SNALR: RN 8 hrs/day 5 days/week, LPN 8 hrs/day the other 2 days, RN on call 24/7, with a waiver option at 40 or fewer beds. Immunization and TB records for EALR/SNALR direct-care staff. Advanced home health aide rules.

citations.title: ALR personnel records (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced in 1001.10(i)(8) and 1001.11(c)(2)(iii), (e) for resident and personnel record content. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: ALR structural and environmental standards
citations.requirement: Additional structural standards for ALRs. SNALR beds must be in a fixed area (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Assisted living definitions (Art. 46-B)
citations.requirement: ALR means 5 or more residents with 24-hour on-site monitoring. ALP is excluded from the definition.

citations.title: Enhanced assisted living certification and aging in place
citations.requirement: EALR certification and aging-in-place rules, including the physician's report.

citations.title: General requirements; fees; quality reporting and price posting
citations.requirement: ALR biennial fee. ALRs must post starting monthly rate, rent range, approved agreement and fee summary on the website and in the facility, and report annual quality measures to DOH. Operating an ALR without approval is a class A misdemeanor (§4656(5)).

citations.title: Establishment of adult care facilities; eligible operators; ownership changes
citations.requirement: Eligible operator structures. DOH approval of LLC articles before filing. Transfer of 10% or more of interests needs prior DOH approval, and smaller transfers need 90 days' notice (§461-b(9)). Operating without approval is a class A misdemeanor (§461-b(2)(d)).

citations.title: Assisted living program (Medicaid)
citations.requirement: ALP eligibility. Requires a LHCSA or CHHA under identical ownership and PHHPC approval. Case-by-case public need review for new beds from April 1, 2025.

citations.title: ALP capitated rate methodology
citations.requirement: ALP capitated rates equal 50% of low-intensity nursing home prices by wage-equalization region.

citations.title: Operating certificates
citations.requirement: Certificate term up to 4 years, non-transferable. Facility may not use a designation not on the certificate (§485.5(f)). 120-day written notice and DOH-approved plan before closure (§485.5(k)).

citations.title: Application for operating certificate
citations.requirement: Part I and Part II approval. Part II must include the disaster plan, admission and residency agreements, personnel policies and service plans. Final inspection requirements.

citations.title: Renewal of operating certificates
citations.requirement: Apply for renewal 45 to 90 days before expiration.

citations.title: Inspections/surveys of adult care facilities
citations.requirement: Cited in the fact-checked research as the basis for recertification surveys every 12 or 18 months. Correct cited violations within 30 days (research checklist).

citations.title: Posting of complaint line and resident rights materials
citations.requirement: Cited in the fact-checked research for posting the DOH ACF complaint line (1-866-893-6772) and resident rights materials. Do Not Refer List consequences.

citations.title: Termination of admission/residency agreements (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cited in 10 NYCRR 1001.10(m)(5) as the statutory proceeding for terminating the residency agreement of a resident who needs 24-hour skilled nursing care. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Justice Center mandated reporting, staff exclusion list, code of conduct (cross-references only)
citations.requirement: Cited inside 18 NYCRR 487.9(a)(3)(vii)-(viii), (a)(7) and (a)(17) and 487.10(i) for reportable incidents, mandated reporters, the staff exclusion list (SSL 495), State Central Register consultation (SSL 424-a) and the Justice Center code of conduct (Exec. Law 554). Statutory text NOT fetched.

citations.title: HIV/bloodborne pathogen exposure definitions (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cited in 10 NYCRR 1001.11(h) as defining significant risk exposure for the ALR exposure prevention program. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Confidential HIV-related information (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cited in 18 NYCRR 487.10(d)(3)-(4) for confidentiality of HIV-related information on residents, employees, volunteers, applicants and prospective residents. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Paid sick leave
citations.requirement: 40 hours of paid sick leave for 5-99 employees, 56 hours for 100+ (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Minimum wage
citations.requirement: From 1/1/2026: $17.00/hr in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester; $16.00/hr elsewhere. General rates stay the same on 1/1/2027. Home care aide minimum for LHCSA aides is $19.65/$18.65 in 2026 and $20.00/$19.00 on 1/1/2027 (per the fact-checked research).

citations.title: Home health aide training (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: Cited in 10 NYCRR 1001.11(n), (p), (r)(2) for home health aide training in EALR/SNALR. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Food service sanitation (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: 10 NYCRR 1001.10(h)(2) requires all food purchasing, storage, preparation and service to comply with Part 14 of Title 10 and local health codes. Part 14 text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Controlled substances and professional misconduct provisions on medication (cross-reference only)
citations.requirement: 10 NYCRR 1001.10(l)(2) requires ALR medication policies to comply with these sections and with 18 NYCRR 487.7(f)/488.7(d). Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Medicaid provider compliance programs
citations.requirement: Not in the fact-checked research and NOT fetched. Included from general knowledge for ALP (Medicaid) billing integrity. Confirm applicability thresholds before citing.

citations.title: Managed long term care (ALP exclusion)
citations.requirement: People enrolled in the assisted living program are not eligible for MLTC (per the fact-checked research).

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Licensure Stack and Regulatory Compliance
state_specifics: An ALR must hold an adult home or enriched housing operating certificate plus an ALR license (5+ residents). EALR and SNALR are add-on certifications, and the ALP is a separate approval.
Operating certificates last up to 4 years, are non-transferable, and may not carry a designation not on the certificate (18 NYCRR 485.5(f)).
Apply for certificate renewal 45-90 days before expiration (18 NYCRR 485.7); pay the ALR biennial fee.
Transfer of 10% or more of ownership interests needs prior DOH approval; smaller transfers need 90 days' notice (SSL 461-b(9)).
Give 120 days' written notice to the regional office and follow a DOH-approved closure plan (485.5(k)).

policies.title: Administrator, Case Manager and Activities Director Qualifications, Hours and Vacancy Notice
state_specifics: No one may be designated administrator without prior written DOH approval (487.9(c)). On duty 20 hrs/week for 24 beds or fewer, 40 hrs/week for 25+ beds. Administrator CE is 60 hours every 2 years.
The administrator may be designated case manager and activities director under 50 beds if qualified; qualified staff are required at 50+ beds.
ALR case manager on site at least 20 hrs/week under 25 beds, scaling to at least 40 hrs/week at 45+ beds (10 NYCRR 1001.11(c)(1)).
Enriched housing: program coordinator plus case manager at 0.5 hr/resident/week (488.9). ALP: designated individual and qualified case manager (494.6).
Notify the regional office within 3 business days of a vacancy in the administrator, case manager, activities director, dietary consultant or health consultant position (487.9(a)(16)).

policies.title: General Staff Orientation (All Employees)
state_specifics: Orientation for every employee, documented (18 NYCRR 487.9(a)(3)-(5)). Include the resident rights statement, emergency and evacuation procedures, and reporting duties.
Orientation includes Justice Center mandated reporting and code of conduct where the facility is subject to the Justice Center.
ALR orientation topics and written job descriptions follow 10 NYCRR 1001.11. Include bloodborne pathogen exposure prevention and the post-exposure procedure.
Staff must speak, read and write English (487.9(a)(13)).
Submit the proposed orientation outline with Part II (Schedule 6, item 3a).

policies.title: Aide and Medication-Staff Initial Training and 12-Month In-Service Schedule
state_specifics: ALR resident aides: 40 hours of initial training on the DOH curriculum (or approved equivalent), 12 hours of in-service each year, and an annual performance assessment with direct observation (1001.11(c)(2)).
Adult home operators submit an in-service plan for personal care staff for approval. New personal care staff complete training within 3 months (487.9(g)(4)-(5)).
Provide a training outline for each job title that gives personal care, home health care or medication help, and a 12-month in-service calendar (Schedule 6, items 3b and 20).
EALR/SNALR home health aide training follows 10 NYCRR 700.2 as cross-referenced in 1001.11 (confirm text).
Keep attendance and competency records in personnel files.

policies.title: Staffing Levels, 24-Hour Supervision, First Aid Coverage and Employee in Charge
state_specifics: 24/7 on-site staff: 1 for census 1-40, 2 for 41-80, 3 for 81-150, 4 for 151-200, plus 1 per additional 60 (487.9(f)(6)).

Minimum hours per resident per week: personal care 3.75 (day and evening), housekeeping 1.0, food service 2.0 (never under 35 hrs/week). Enriched housing combined personal care, housekeeping and food is 6 hrs/resident/week (488.9).
At least one first-aid-trained person on site every shift; name the employee in charge when the administrator or coordinator is absent.
The schedule lists all departments and shifts for every day of the week; keep schedules 12 months (487.9(a)(6)).
EALR/SNALR: RN 8 hrs/day 5 days/week, LPN 8 hrs/day on the other 2 days, RN on call 24/7 (waiver possible at 40 or fewer beds).

policies.title: Resident Services Program: Philosophy, Goals and Scope
state_specifics: Minimum services: room, board, housekeeping, supervision, personal care, case management and activities (487.7(a)).
ALR services: housing, 24-hour on-site monitoring, daily food service, case management, ISP, and personal care and/or home care (1001.10).
Residents may use outside providers and choose their own health care providers.
List the cultural, spiritual, diversional, physical, political, social and intellectual activities provided by the facility and the community.
Monthly weights and personal care follow 487.7(e).

policies.title: Resident Rights, Responsibilities and Ombudsman/Legal Services Access
state_specifics: Rights statement (19 minimum rights) is posted, given at admission and reviewed with residents annually (487.5(a)).
Applicants get the rights statement, admission agreement, facility rules and the Ombudsman/legal-services sheet at or before the admission interview (487.4).
Post the DOH ACF complaint line 1-866-893-6772 and the resident rights materials (SSL 460-d).
Residents may meet and communicate privately with the Ombudsman and advocates; keep contact information posted.
Collect a signed acknowledgment of the rights statement at admission and annually.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Written grievance system; post the procedure (487.5(c)).
Post the DOH complaint line 1-866-893-6772 beside the procedure.
Keep a grievance log with date, response, resolution and administrator review.
Report grievance trends to the QA committee (see GOV-02).
Residents may take grievances to the resident organization.

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: Emergency and illness response duties follow 487.7(d); document each event and notify the resident's physician and representative.
Complete the Incident Report when 487.7(d) triggers apply.
Retention is limited by the 487.4 exclusions (for example continual medical or nursing care). EALR/SNALR have a 24-hour skilled nursing retention exception (1001.10).
If a resident can no longer be retained, make persistent efforts at alternative placement (487.4).
Re-evaluate and update the ISP after any significant change (ties to AD-03).

policies.title: Personal Care, Falls Prevention and Skin Integrity
state_specifics: Personal care per 487.7(e): physical restraints are banned and weights are taken monthly.
Personal care staffing: at least 3.75 hrs/resident/week on day and evening shifts (487.9(g)).
Falls with injury or other incident triggers are reported on the Incident Report (487.7(d)). Review falls in QA.
Skin checks and fall-risk review are part of the case manager evaluation, at least every 12 months and on change of condition.
Refer to the physician or a home care/nursing provider for pressure injuries; document the referral.

policies.title: Hospice, Home Health Coordination and Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Health services come from an Article 36 home care agency unless the facility is EALR/SNALR-approved (1001.10).
Hospice is permitted without EALR when the conditions in 1001.10 are met.
Death, suicide attempts and felonies are reported as required by 487.7(d).
Coordinate in writing with the hospice or home care agency on the ISP, medications and emergency contacts.
After a death, secure belongings and funds per FUN-01 and follow the notification steps in 487.7(d).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Confidentiality of HIV-related information on residents, employees, volunteers and applicants follows 18 NYCRR 485.11(g)(9)-(15), cross-referenced in 487.10(d)(3)-(4).
Resident records are kept secure and released only as permitted by law or with consent.
Designate a privacy officer and train all staff at orientation.
Give residents a notice of privacy practices if the facility is a HIPAA covered entity.
ALP and EALR/SNALR services may make the operator a covered entity; confirm with counsel.

policies.title: Optional Resident Services (Respite, Social Day Care, Non-ACF Space Use), Special Services and Transportation
state_specifics: State in Schedule 6 whether the facility will offer respite or social day care (Schedule 7D application required for social day care).
Using part of an adult home for non-ACF purposes (e.g., an outside provider's medical office) requires a waiver request for 487.11(l)(1).
Describe every special service (e.g., podiatry, therapies, outside vendors) and who provides it.
Transportation: describe how residents get to medical appointments and activities, and who pays.
Respite residents follow the admission and medical evaluation rules in AD-02.

policies.title: Admission and Retention Standards and Resident Profile
state_specifics: Do not admit or retain any of the 13 excluded groups in 487.4 (e.g., continual medical or nursing care, chronically bedfast, chronic unmanaged incontinence, danger to self or others).
Describe the resident profile and any target populations (e.g., dementia, 65+) for Schedule 6.
EALR permits aging in place with a physician's report (PHL 4655).
SNALR admits residents with special needs under the approved plan only.
ALR is 5 or more residents with 24-hour on-site monitoring (PHL 4651).

policies.title: Pre-Admission Evaluation and Admission Interview
state_specifics: Medical evaluation (DSS-3122) within 30 days before admission and at least every 12 months (487.4).
Written administrator interview before admission.
ALR case manager evaluation before admission and at least every 12 months, using the DOH personal data and resident evaluation form (1001.10).
Give the applicant the agreement, rights statement, rules and Ombudsman/legal-services sheet at or before the interview; offer the latest DOH inspection report.
Document the decision and the reasons for any denial.

policies.title: Individualized Service Plan (ISP) and Reassessment
state_specifics: ALRs must have an ISP for each resident (1001.10; cross-referenced to 1001.7, confirm subdivision before citing).
The case manager evaluates before admission and at least every 12 months.
Update the ISP on change of condition and share it with the resident, representative and outside providers.
Submit the ISP form and process with Schedule 6, item 7d.
Adult home case management duties follow 487.7.

policies.title: Palliative Care (EALR/SNALR) and Advance Directives
state_specifics: EALR and SNALR applicants must submit a palliative care policy.
Hospice is permitted when the conditions in 1001.10 are met.
Ask about advance directives at admission, record them in the chart and honor them. Confirm the NY statutory citations for health care proxy and MOLST before publishing.
Review goals of care at each reassessment and on change of condition.
Coordinate with hospice and the resident's physician.

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Deposits, Price Posting and Refunds
state_specifics: Use the DOH model admission/residency agreement and the EALR, SNALR and ALP addenda; agreements are pre-approved in Part II.
Admission agreement content follows 487.5(d), including the SSI/HR personal allowance offer and refunds.
ALRs post the starting monthly rate, rent range, approved agreement and fee summary on the website and in the facility (PHL 4656).
The ALR agreement lists services and additional charges (1001.8, cross-reference; confirm text).
2026 SSI Congregate Care Level 3 is $1,688/month; the resident keeps $262 for personal needs.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Termination Notice
state_specifics: 30 days' written notice on the DOH form, with a list of free legal and advocacy services (487.5(f)).
Send a copy to the regional office within 5 days.
A court proceeding is required if the resident objects.
Make persistent efforts at alternative placement (487.4).
Termination for 24-hour skilled nursing need in an ALR follows SSL 461-h as cross-referenced in 1001.10(m)(5) (confirm text).

policies.title: Resident Fund Accounts, Funds and Personal Property
state_specifics: Must offer resident fund accounts to SSI and SNA recipients even if the facility does not accept SSI/SNA as payment in full.
Handle resident funds and valuables per 18 NYCRR 487.6 (confirm subdivisions before citing).
2026 SSI Congregate Care Level 3 is $1,688/month ($994 federal + $694 state); the resident keeps $262.
Provide a Resident Fund Account Statement to residents (Schedule 6 item 31).
Admission agreement states the personal allowance offer and refund terms (487.5(d)).

policies.title: Mental Health Services Agreement and Coordination
state_specifics: Schedule 6, section 9 requires a mental health agreement. Confirm the exact form and requirements with the regional office.
Describe how residents with mental health needs are referred and followed.
Ties to the exclusions in 487.4 (danger to self or others).
Record contacts and crisis steps in the ISP.

policies.title: Disaster and Emergency Plan, Evacuation and DOH Notifications
state_specifics: Written plan approved by DOH (487.12), including evacuation procedures; reviewed in Part II.
Notify DOH by the next business day of a work stoppage, fire, loss of a fire system, no hot water or loss of essential services.
Keep a Health Commerce (HPN) account with 24/7 contacts and update it monthly.
Address residents with mobility, cognitive and sensory needs.
Review the plan at least annually and after each event.

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: Monthly staff fire drills at varied times, with full and partial evacuation (487.12).
Quarterly drills with residents and one total evacuation every 12 months.
Fire authorities, a certified service agency or DOH observe a resident drill annually.
Keep drill records.
Sprinklers are required throughout buildings of 25+ beds (487.11).

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Medication management follows 487.7(f) (adult home) and 488.7(d) (enriched housing), as required for ALRs by 1001.10(l).
Residents may self-administer; staff assistance is limited; store medications securely.
No dose changes without physician authorization.
Apply for a Class 3A limited controlled substance license before the regional office on-site inspection.
Controlled substance rules in 10 NYCRR 80.5-80.6 (cross-reference; confirm text).

policies.title: Medication Assistance, Staff Authorization and Records
state_specifics: Staff may only provide assistance within 487.7(f) limits; no injectables by staff except licensed staff.
Keep a medication assistance record and follow the PRN rules in 1001.10.
Only trained and authorized staff assist with medications (see ORI-02).
In EALR/SNALR, nursing services are delivered by RN/LPN per 1001.11.
Report medication errors on the Incident Report and notify the physician.

policies.title: EALR Skilled Nursing and Home Health Services, Nursing Coverage and Delegation
state_specifics: Submit policies for all skilled nursing services and HHA services beyond resident care aide scope to be delivered by operator staff. The list must match the EALR addendum.
Additions or deletions to EALR services need prior regional office approval.
RN on site 8 hrs/day 5 days/week, LPN 8 hrs/day the other 2 days, RN on call 24/7 (1001.11).
Waiver of the on-site minimum may be requested at 40 or fewer beds.
Immunization and TB records for EALR/SNALR direct-care staff.

policies.title: SNALR Dementia Unit Plan, Memory Care and Wandering Safeguards
state_specifics: Submit the dementia unit/SNALR plan; DOH publishes a SNALR plan guide.
SNALR beds must be in a fixed area (1001.13).
Include staffing, dementia training, environment and wander safeguards (see SAF-02).
Same RN/LPN coverage as EALR (1001.11).
Include family organization policies (see ORG-01).

policies.title: SNALR Activities Schedule
state_specifics: Submit a dementia unit/SNALR activities schedule with Schedule 6.
Activities must fit residents' cognitive abilities and be offered daily, including evenings and weekends.
Staff the activities and record participation.
Review the schedule at least quarterly.

policies.title: ALP Referral Sources, Co-located Beds and Site Description
state_specifics: Describe anticipated sources of referral and discharge for the ALP and the proposed relationship with each.
If the ALP is in the same building as non-ALP adult home or enriched housing beds, describe how the programs relate.
Describe the proposed site, including physical relationship with and access to community services.
ALP requires a LHCSA or CHHA under identical ownership and PHHPC approval for a new LHCSA (SSL 461-l).
New ALP beds are approved case by case on public need from April 1, 2025.

policies.title: ALP Services, Capitated Rate and Medicaid Compliance
state_specifics: Services in the Medicaid capitated rate follow 18 NYCRR 494.5; staffing follows 494.6 (designated individual, qualified case manager, minimum staffing per 487.9(f)(6)).
Rates are 50% of low-intensity nursing home prices by wage region (PHL 3614(6)).
ALP residents are not eligible for MLTC (PHL 4403-f).
Compliance program per SSL 363-d and 18 NYCRR Part 521 (confirm applicability thresholds).
Screen staff against exclusion lists (see PER-02); send rate questions to ALP-Rates@health.ny.gov.

policies.title: Personnel Policies: Rules of Conduct, Hiring, Termination, Employee Grievances and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Written rules of conduct, hiring and termination policies, and an employee grievance procedure.
Staff must speak, read and write English (487.9(a)(13)).
Justice Center code of conduct applies where the facility is subject to the Justice Center (Exec. Law 554, cross-reference).
Resident volunteers and employees are governed by 487.9(b).
Include professional boundaries: no gifts, loans, financial dealings or personal relationships with residents.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Run criminal history record checks for direct-care staff (487.9(a)(7)).
Check the Justice Center Staff Exclusion List and the State Central Register before hiring if subject to the Justice Center (487.9(a)(17)).
Check federal exclusion lists for ALP/Medicaid-funded staff.
Keep results in personnel files.
Re-check on the schedule you set, at least annually (policy).

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Before employment and every 12 months: a physician/PA/RN statement of fitness and a TB risk assessment/testing (487.9(a)(8)).
EALR/SNALR direct-care staff need immunization and TB records (1001.11).
ALR bloodborne pathogen exposure prevention and post-exposure procedure (1001.11(h)).
Keep health records separate from personnel files.

policies.title: Personnel Records and Staffing Schedules
state_specifics: Maintain personnel records per 487.9(a)(7); ALR content per 1001.12 (cross-reference; confirm).
Keep staffing schedules 12 months (487.9(a)(6)).
Document orientation, in-service and competency.
Retention period for personnel records: confirm against 487.10(h) (7 years for program and business records).

policies.title: Workers' Compensation, Wages and Paid Sick Leave
state_specifics: Carry workers' compensation, disability and paid family leave coverage.
2026 minimum wage: $17.00 in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester; $16.00 elsewhere.
ALP LHCSA aides: home care aide minimum $19.65 downstate and $18.65 elsewhere in 2026, $20.00/$19.00 from 1/1/2027.
Paid sick leave: 40 hours for 5-99 employees, 56 hours for 100+ (Labor Law 196-b).

policies.title: Job Descriptions for All Staff Positions
state_specifics: Written job description for every position, including administrator, case manager, aides, food service, housekeeping and maintenance.
For EALR and ALP that employ HHAs, list the tasks HHAs may perform, within HHA scope.
ALR requires written job descriptions (1001.11).
Give each employee a copy at hire and review annually.

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Activities are a required minimum service (487.7(a)).
Submit a one-month activity schedule with Schedule 6.
The administrator may be activities director under 50 beds if qualified.
Offer a mix of cultural, spiritual, physical, social and intellectual activities and record attendance.

policies.title: Social Contact and Visitors
state_specifics: Describe how the facility encourages contact among residents, relatives and friends.
Visitor access is consistent with the resident rights statement.
Support phone, mail, video calls and community outings.
Share the visitor policy at the admission interview.

policies.title: House Rules (Smoking, Pets, Quiet Hours)
state_specifics: Give house rules to applicants at or before the admission interview (487.4).
Rules must not conflict with the resident rights statement.
Cover smoking, pets, alcohol and guest rules.
Submit house rules with Schedule 6 if any.

policies.title: Resident Organization and SNALR Family Organization
state_specifics: Residents may form an organization (487.5(b)); the administrator provides meeting space and responds to its input.
SNALR: policy for a family organization.
Record meetings and responses.

policies.title: Menus, Therapeutic and Modified Diets, and Diet Information for Kitchen Staff
state_specifics: Submit 3 weeks of menus for meals and snacks, including modified diets (finger foods, consistency modifications), diet definitions and service times.
Kitchen staff must have current diet orders, allergies, preferences and changes for each resident.
A qualified dietitian or dietetic technician supervises food service under a written agreement stating duties and time (487.9(j)(3)-(4)).
Food service staff: 2.0 hrs/resident/week, never under 35 hrs/week.
Daily food service is an ALR minimum service (1001.10).

policies.title: Food Purchasing, Storage, Temperature Control and Food Protection
state_specifics: All food purchasing, storage, preparation and service comply with 10 NYCRR Part 14 and local health codes (1001.10(h)(2)); confirm Part 14 text.
Log refrigerator, freezer and hot-holding temperatures.
Protect meals and snacks from contamination; label and date stored items.

policies.title: Food Service Staff Training
state_specifics: Food service staff complete orientation and in-service, documented (487.9(a)(3)-(5)).
Training covers sanitation (Part 14), diets, allergies and safe temperatures.
Keep training records.

policies.title: Volunteers
state_specifics: Volunteers receive orientation covering rights, confidentiality (including HIV-related information) and emergency procedures.
Volunteers are supervised and do not count toward required staffing hours (facility policy).
Resident volunteers follow 487.9(b).

policies.title: Resident and Facility Records and Retention
state_specifics: Resident and facility records per 487.10(c)-(d).
Retention: individual records 3 years after death or discharge; program, business and renewal records 7 years (487.10(h)).
Use mandated forms and keep required postings (487.10(f)-(g)).
ALR record content per 1001.10(i)(8) and 1001.12.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Annual financial statement DSS-2963, quarterly statistical report and quarterly resident roster (487.10(e)).
Incident Report per 487.7(d); next-business-day DOH notifications per 487.12.
Justice Center reportable incidents immediately (487.14).
ALR annual quality measures and price posting (PHL 4656).
Notify the regional office of key vacancies within 3 business days.

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance Plans
state_specifics: Housekeeping: at least 1.0 hr/resident/week (487.9(h)).
Environmental standards: bedrooms 100 sq ft single and 160 sq ft double, 1 toilet per 6 and 1 bath per 10 residents, call system, sprinklers at 25+ beds (487.11).
ALR structural standards in 1001.13.
Preventive maintenance schedule: fire systems, water temperature, call system, HVAC.
Maintain written logs for inspections and repairs.

policies.title: Non-Discrimination, Reasonable Accommodation and Language Access
state_specifics: Include a non-discrimination statement and a reasonable accommodation policy in admission procedures, consistent with DAL DACF 23-15.
Provide interpreter and translation help for limited-English residents.
Admission decisions are based on 487.4 criteria only.

policies.title: Quality Assurance, Survey Readiness and Posting
state_specifics: QA plan updated at least every two years; quality improvement committee meets at least every six months (487.10(d)(5)(ix)).
Recertification surveys every 12 or 18 months; correct cited violations within 30 days.
Post the DOH complaint line 1-866-893-6772.
ALRs report annual quality measures to DOH.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Facilities subject to the Justice Center and their mandated reporters report reportable incidents immediately on reasonable cause (487.14).
The facility must start an investigation.
Staff Exclusion List and State Central Register checks (see PER-02).
Residents may call the DOH complaint line or the Ombudsman.
Protect reporters from retaliation (facility policy).

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting, Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Incident Report triggers, missing-resident steps, and death, suicide attempt and felony reporting follow 487.7(d).
Notify DOH by the next business day for events listed in 487.12.
Search procedure, who to call and when to alert police.
Wander-risk assessment and safeguards for dementia residents.
Review incidents in QA.

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Physical restraints are prohibited (487.7(e)).
Use least-restrictive alternatives and document behavior-management approaches.
Locked areas apply only to an approved SNALR/fixed area.
Any suspected restraint use is reported as an incident.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Bloodborne pathogen exposure program and post-exposure procedure (1001.11(h)).
Employee TB screening (487.9(a)(8)).
Define significant risk exposure per 10 NYCRR 63 (cross-reference; confirm).
Outbreak reporting to the local health department as required by law.
Hand hygiene, cleaning and laundry procedures.

documents.title: Adult Care Facility Common Application – Schedule 6, Program Information (Part II) – Regional Office
documents.issuer: New York State Department of Health (Regional Office Part II review; Central Office project manager copied)
documents.how_used: This is the official Part II program-review checklist. It applies to new adult homes and enriched housing programs, changes of operator, and new ALR, EALR, SNALR and ALP applications. The ALR and ALP applicant instructions say to submit only changed or new materials and to check 'No Change' where applicable. The 'required_items' list below uses the form's own item numbers. I left out paperwork that is not policy content: item 1 (application type check-boxes), item 2 (administrator/coordinator qualifications on DSS-3233, diplomas and transcripts), item 9 (Mental Health Agreement), item 12 (list of forms), item 15d–15f (support letters, nursing-facility transfer agreement, DSS contract), item 16 (waiver and equivalency list), item 18 (workers' compensation certificate), item 26(b)–(d) (dietary consultant agreement, resume and licenses), item 26(f) (kitchen and dining room diagram), and item 31 (resident fund account statement).

documents.title: Adult Care Facility and Assisted Living Common Application (landing page; applications are submitted via NYSECON, see DAL #19-16)
documents.issuer: NYS DOH Bureau of Licensure and Certification
documents.version: Current web page. It says applications must be submitted via NYSECON effective July 1, 2019.
documents.how_used: Context for how the submission is made. Schedules 1–5 are reviewed by Central Office for Part I approval. Schedule 6 is reviewed by the Regional Office for Part II approval. Part I and Part II may be reviewed at the same time, and final approval needs both. Model documents, such as the model residency agreements, are posted on this page.

required_items.text: Staff Orientation and Aide Training: Submit a copy of your proposed general staff orientation to be used for all employees.
Staff Orientation and Aide Training: Submit a copy of the initial training required for each job title that provides personal care, home health care and/or medication services.

Planned Staffing Schedule: Submit planned staffing schedule to be implemented upon approval of this application. Include: Adequate staffing for each shift on each day of the week; Persons trained in first aid (one of which must be scheduled for each shift); and The employee in charge for each shift when the administrator or program coordinator is absent; and All employees in all departments.

Resident Services: Describe philosophy, goals, and scope of your resident service program. (List cultural, spiritual, diversional, physical, political, social and intellectual activities to be provided by facility and community.)

Optional Resident Services: Applicant wishes to offer or continue a respite program; Applicant wishes to offer or continue a social day care program (see Schedule 7D); Applicant plans to use a portion of the requested adult home for purposes other than the operation of an adult care facility such as to house medical office for outside providers (submit a waiver request for section 487.11(l)(1)). For a change of operator application, the Schedule 7D applications for the social day care program must be submitted to continue the previous operator's respite or social day care programs.
Admission Policies (all applicants): admission and retention standards
Admission Policies (all applicants): resident profile that includes a description of any target populations
Admission Policies (all applicants): pre-admission evaluation policy
If you are applying for an Assisted Living Residence, also submit: ISP form, policy and process
If you are applying for an Assisted Living Residence, also submit: Palliative Care Policy (EALR and SNALR)
Resident Fund Accounts. NOTE: You must offer resident fund accounts for residents who are SSI and/or SNA recipients, even if you do not accept SSI/SNA as payment in full.
Disaster and Emergency Plan: Submit a copy of your disaster and emergency plan, including evacuation procedures.

Medication Management Policies and Procedures. NOTE: Applicant must apply for a Class 3A limited controlled substance license. This is typically done just prior to the regional office's on-site inspection.

EALR Policies and Procedures: For EALR only, submit copies of all policies and procedures for skilled nursing services and those HHA services above and beyond what resident care aides may deliver, to be delivered directly by Operator's staff. This list of policies must match the list of services in your EALR addendum. Any addition or deletion of EALR services must be prior approved by the regional office.
SNALR Policies and Procedures: For SNALRs only, submit a copy of your: dementia unit/SNALR plan
SNALR Policies and Procedures: For SNALRs only, submit a copy of your: dementia unit/SNALR activities schedule
ALP Program Information (newly established ALPs): Describe the anticipated sources of referral to, and discharge from, the ALP and describe the proposed relationship with these sources.
ALP Program Information: Will the ALP be located in the same building with non-ALP adult home or enriched housing beds? If yes, describe how the ALP will relate to these services programmatically.
ALP Program Information: Describe the proposed site for the ALP including physical relationship with and access to community services.
Personnel Policies and Procedures: Include the following: rules of conduct, facility policy regarding grievance procedures, hiring and termination policies.
Job Descriptions for all staff positions: For EALRs and ALPS that employ Home Health Aides (HHAs), include the tasks that HHAs are authorized to perform, which must be within the HHA scope of tasks.
In-Service Training, 12 month in-service schedule
Activity Schedule for One Month
Social Contact: A description of how the facility will encourage contact between residents, relatives and friends.
House Rules, if any
Resident Organizations and, if SNALR, Family Organization Policies
A Description of Special Services, if any

Food Services, including: three weeks of menus for meals and snacks, including the special modified diets offered including diets such as finger foods and consistency modifications, and a definition of each diet offered. Include the times of each meal and snack service
Food Services, including: policy and procedure for kitchen staff to have current and accurate information regarding each resident's prescribed diet, allergies, food preferences and any changes.
Food Services, including: policy and procedure for food purchase and storage.
Food Services, including: policy and procedure to ensure meals and snacks are handled properly to ensure proper temperatures and other food protections.
Food Services, including: policy on food service staff training.
Volunteer Policy and Orientation, if volunteers are to be used in the facility
Record Keeping policy for maintaining records and reports
Housekeeping Plan
Maintenance Plan

Any entity applying to operate an ACF or certify additional beds in an ACF must develop and submit admission procedures and policies, including a non-discrimination statement and reasonable accommodation policy, consistent with ACF DAL# DACF 23-15.

official.notes: The reviewer is the DOH Regional Office for the county where the facility is or will be. Each of the 32 items on DOH-5098 is a numbered section, and the manual should follow that numbering. For each item, the applicant gives an attachment number or checks 'No Change' (on items that have that box). The ALR and ALP instructions limit responses to changed or new materials. Items 13 (EALR), 14 (SNALR) and 15 (ALP) apply only to those license types. Item 15 is completed in full (15a–15f) for a newly established ALP. For a change of operator, only 15e–15f are completed. The completed Schedule 6 is submitted with a cover letter to the regional office, with a copy of the cover letter to the assigned Central Office project manager in Albany. It can be submitted at any time, but no later than 90 days after the Part I approval notice. Applications go in through NYSECON. Any substitute for a DOH-mandated form must be listed under item 12 and needs an equivalency (see item 16). Model documents, such as the model residency agreements, are posted on the Common Application web page. Items 17, 20 and 26 spell out their own sub-requirements, so keep that wording inside those sections. The regulations cited in the request (18 NYCRR Parts 487, 488 and 494; 10 NYCRR Part 1001) set the substantive standards behind these items. Schedule 6 is the single official checklist used for the review, so I did not pull items from those regulations.
